top_categories.workout_context: 1504 miles. Your legs will beg to quit after 120. This trains the power output you need from mile 130 onward.
Race-pace efforts that mimic TransAtlanticWay's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before June.
At TransAtlanticWay, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
88,583ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
59ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.

Road-specific control matters at TransAtlanticWay. Practice on mixed mountain-pass and coastal terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 1504 miles.
1504 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 88,583ft of climbing on mixed mountain-pass and coastal terrain does to your power file on race day.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 1504 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of TransAtlanticWay. Train it until it feels boring.
Low-cadence force work supports 88,583ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
88,583ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.

race_overlay.nutrition: For a multi-day 1504-mile race, no single calorie total or one-food strategy is credible. Rehearse continuous intake while riding plus substantial meals at planned stops; document carbohydrate, fluid, and sodium intake, resupply cadence, and gut response. Use checkpoints and publicly available services only as the category rules allow, carry backup calories, and complete a full night-riding systems rehearsal.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at TransAtlanticWay rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on mixed mountain-pass and coastal terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, Race Simulation, and Over Under to prepare you for 1504 miles of mixed mountain-pass and coastal terrain in Cork/Kinsale to Derry, Ireland.
